links.outcome: Expert-rated quality of retrieval-augmented systems versus general-purpose LLMs on periodontal vignettes
links.effect: Retrieval-augmented systems rated highest (Perplexity, OpenEvidence and Claude 4.7 Opus formed a top tier), but the advantage was confounded with response length.
links.quote: Retrieval-augmented systems rated highest, but this advantage was confounded with response length.

links.outcome: Proportion of responses with at least one parameter scored dangerous (<=2) by blinded periodontists
links.effect: At least one parameter scored dangerous (<=2) in 3.3%-46.7% of responses across platforms, despite mean composite scores of 3.28-4.86.
links.quote: At least one parameter scored dangerous (≤ 2) in 3.3%-46.7% of responses across platforms, despite mean composite scores (3.28-4.86) exceeding the rubric midpoint of 3.0.

screen.reason: The study empirically tests whether adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) platforms compares favorably to standard general-purpose LLMs on clinical safety and accuracy using periodontal clinical vignettes.
